guidance: Preliminary engineering estimate—verify loads, materials, governing standards, and calculations with a qualified engineer before fabrication or construction.
method: The contact pressure of a press or shrink fit follows from Lamé's thick-walled cylinder solution: the hub is a cylinder pressed on its inside, the shaft one pressed on its outside, and the two elastic deflections together must absorb the diametral interference. With d the fit diameter, D the hub outside diameter, di the shaft bore (zero for a solid shaft), E and ν the moduli and Poisson's ratios, and the subscripts o and i for hub and shaft, the pressure is p = δ / { d [ ((D²+d²)/(D²−d²) + νo)/Eo + ((d²+di²)/(d²−di²) − νi)/Ei ] }, which for a 50 mm solid steel shaft in a 90 mm steel hub with 40 µm of interference gives 58.07 MPa. The hub carries a tensile hoop stress p(D²+d²)/(D²−d²) at its bore and 2pd²/(D²−d²) at its outside, and with the radial stress −p its bore von Mises stress is p√(k²+k+1) for that bore ratio k; the safety factor divides the hub yield strength by it. The shaft is in compression: a solid shaft sits under uniform hydrostatic pressure −p, so its von Mises stress equals p, while a hollow shaft is most stressed at its bore. Friction over the contact area πdL carries an axial slip force F = μpπdL and a torque T = Fd/2 = μpπd²L/2. That same friction force is what a press must supply while the parts slide, because once they are seated the pressure comes from the interference and not from the press. Heating only the hub opens the bore by αdΔT, so the interference alone needs ΔT = δ/(αd) and a 20 µm slip clearance needs (δ + 0.02 mm)/(αd). Because the pressure is linear in the interference, doubling the interference doubles the holding capacity and the bore stress together. Inputs are bounded: fit diameter 1 to 5000 mm, hub outside diameter above the fit diameter up to 10000 mm, shaft bore from 0 to just under the fit diameter, diametral interference 0.1 to 5000 µm, engagement 1 to 5000 mm, friction 0.01 to 1.5, moduli 1 to 1000 GPa, Poisson's ratios 0 to 0.49, hub expansion 0.1 to 50 × 10⁻⁶/°C and hub yield 10 to 3000 MPa. This is a linear-elastic, plane-stress estimate of a single cylindrical fit: it ignores surface roughness and taper, centrifugal growth and service temperature differences, edge stress concentration, fretting and fatigue, and the plastic redistribution that begins once the bore yields, so it is preliminary sizing rather than a design review. Everything runs locally in the browser.

sources.title: Formulas for interference (press and shrink) fit calculations (AmesWeb): interference pressure from the diametral interference, hub and shaft hoop stresses and the von Mises stress at the hub surface
